transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-01-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Tom Reynolds (OakGrove CTO), Maya Lopez (Head of ML), Jamal Carter (Lead DevOps), Aisha Khan (Security)
Shared: implementation-runbook-v1 (link), security-pack (link: https://redwood.ai/sec-pack/oakgrove)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align scope for implementation sprint 1, validate networking/auth requirements for Private VPC deployment option, confirm success criteria and timeline for pilot (ingest -> embeddings -> retrieval -> inference in staging).

Topics Covered:
- Deployment mode: Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Data residency and KMS/HSM key management
- Network egress, peering, and firewall requirements
- Model selection, quantization, and perf targets (latency SLOs)
- Rollout plan and ramp to prod

Transcript:
[00:00] Sasha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Sasha, account lead for OakGrove. Marco and Priya are with me from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:18] Tom: Hi all, Tom Reynolds, CTO at OakGrove. We're excited to get started.
[00:25] Maya: Maya here, head of ML, I'll own model-validation and quality metrics.
[00:31] Jamal: Jamal, DevOps — I'll handle networking and infra.
[00:34] Aisha: Aisha from security/compliance, will be focused on SOC2 and KMS questions.
[00:40] Marco: Great, thanks. I'll run through the implementation plan and technical checklist then we can dig in.
[00:46] Sasha: High level — goal is pilot in 6 weeks, prove latency < 200ms p50 on our user flows and keep token costs predictable.
[00:56] Tom: That sounds right, our current baseline is around 350ms p50 on our homegrown endpoint so anything under 200 is a win.
[01:05] Marco: Cool. First question: are you planning to go Hosted or Private? I know earlier thread mentioned Private VPC due to data residency.
[01:14] Maya: We prefer Private VPC for customer data. Some datasets are sensitive. Also want to use our KMS keys.
[01:20] Aisha: Yep, we'll need KMS integration and want audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. SOC two requirements.
[01:28] Marco: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS keys, HSM integrations. The audit log forwarding is supported — we can set up a collector to push to your Splunk or S3. There may be a short config step.
[01:41] Jamal: For peering, do you support cross-account VPC peering or do we need a transit gateway?
[01:47] Marco: We support both patterns; for scale we usually recommend transit gateway for multi-AZ. We'll share a network diagram.
[01:54] Sasha: Action item — Marco will share network topology options and a sample peering template.
[02:01] Marco: I'll paste that into the shared runbook after the call.
[02:05] Tom: On model side — we have a custom fine-tuned open model and are evaluating quantization. Is Redwood able to serve customer models pinned to versions?
[02:14] Marco: Yes, we support version pinning and rollout policies. For quantized weights — we recommend 4-bit with per-layer calibration for that model family, but we need to run a perf/quality sweep.
[02:24] Maya: Important for us: no quality regressions. We'll run evaluation sets and want alerts if regression > 1% F1 drop.
[02:30] Marco: We can integrate your eval harness into Redwood Optimize; will surface regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[02:37] Sasha: Next, latency budget — you said p50 under 200ms; do you have p95 or tail requirements?
[02:44] Tom: p95 under 450ms ideally. Consistency matters more than low tail.
[02:50] Marco: That's helpful. On Dedicated capacity we can guarantee throughput, but tails can be helped with warm pools and autoscale. For Private you get more control but you need to size the GPU pool.
[03:00] Jamal: For sizing we'll need a throughput estimate — concurrent requests and tokens per request.
[03:05] Maya: Typical user request is ~120 tokens generation, concurrency ~20 peak.
[03:11] Marco: Great, that'll help model estimate. We'll include a suggested instance mix in the sizing doc.
[03:18] Aisha: Security question — do you persist raw customer inputs in logs? We need strict retention policies.
[03:25] Priya: Hi, Priya here — by default Redwood retains minimal logs and you can configure retention or disable storing raw inputs for Private deploy. We'll also do role-based access control.
[03:36] Aisha: And SSO? We need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[03:40] Marco: SAML/SCIM supported; we'll include the SSO config steps.
[03:45] Tom: Is there a way to test egress rules before we open prod? We prefer a staging validation window.
[03:51] Marco: Yes, we'll set up a staging VPC and provide test endpoints. Expect a smoke test checklist.
[03:57] Sasha: Let's talk timelines — we want pilot in 6 weeks. Does that feel realistic?
[04:03] Marco: With your team aligned on KMS and network it is. Typical sprint plan: week 1 network and infra, week 2 model onboarding and small perf run, week 3 eval & optimization, week 4 integrate with harness, week 5 staging validation, week 6 pilot.
[04:19] Maya: That lines up. We'll need Redwood to run a perf run against our eval set — can you do that?
[04:25] Marco: Yes, we'll run perf + quality. We'll need a sanitized model bundle and a subset of eval prompts.
[04:31] Tom: Who owns the benchmark orchestration? We can run client side but prefer Redwood to run a baseline for fair comparison.
[04:37] Marco: Redwood SE will run and share raw logs and summary. Expect some noise in transcripts — I mean logs :)
[04:43] Jamal: Any blockers you're aware of?
[04:45] Sasha: Biggest risk is KMS permissions and network peering timing. So prioritize that.
[04:50] Aisha: Also regulatory: we need to prove that no customer PII leaves our VPC in processing. Any mapping for that?
[04:57] Marco: For private we can ensure data plane stays in your VPC, and for hosted we do data handling controls. We'll document the data flow.
[05:06] Priya: I'll drop the security pack and SOC2 artifact links into the shared folder after call.
[05:12] Tom: Great. About cost: how do we predict token spend for the pilot?
[05:17] Sasha: We'll provide cost estimates based on the token profile you gave (120 tokens, concurrency 20). Also Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and cache settings to reduce unit cost.
[05:27] Maya: On caching, can you support prefix/KV cache for session-based chat?
[05:31] Marco: We support KV cache and prefix caching; can enable on model side. We'll propose cache TTLs depending on your freshness needs.
[05:38] Jamal: For infra automation, do you provide Terraform modules?
[05:42] Marco: Yes, Terraform modules for VPC peering, IAM roles and the deployment. We'll share a repo link.
[05:48] Sasha: Let's capture next steps and owners quickly — Priya will create the onboarding channel; Marco share network and sizing docs; Tom provide KMS contacts and compliance list.
[05:58] Maya: One more question — what about canary deploys and automatic rollback?
[06:03] Marco: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variant on quality or error regressions. We'll help configure thresholds.
[06:11] Aisha: Please include evidence of encryption in transit and at rest for the runbook.
[06:16] Priya: We'll add the encryption checklist and a pointer to KMS configuration examples.
[06:22] Tom: Ok if we aim to meet the 6‑week pilot, propose first infra validation on Feb 6th.
[06:29] Sasha: We'll schedule that.
[06:31] Marco: Final note — I'll need a sanitized model artifact and a small eval pack by Feb 2 to meet the perf run schedule.
[06:39] Maya: We'll prioritize that.
[06:41] Sasha: Thanks everyone. Recap of action items will be in calendar invite notes. Any other Qs?
[06:48] Tom: No, thanks folks.
[06:50] Sasha: Great, we'll follow up with the runbook and security pack.
[06:54] Priya: I'll set up the slack channel and add next steps.

End of call.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV cash, SOC two) are present; names sometimes simplified. Short links and internal repo mentions are referenced but not included inline to preserve security.
